Do not stamp. Parent may split this file further if the drop cannot land in one PR. CARRIED FROM W5-G1 (PR 596), established by measurement with its control -- read this before sizing the tranche. (1) THE CENSUS IS 516, NOT 427. Measured by the typing job under the pinned ruler; the 8e99ad1 per-module figures above are carryovers and the tree is 53 .py files against the 48 they were taken over. Re-measure; the ratchet in tests/typing_budgets.json pins what CI measured, never the number in this brief. (2) THERE IS NO PER-MODULE FIGURE IN THE TREE, ON PURPOSE. by_module is emitted by tests/typing_ruler.py into the typing job's log and its typing-census artifact and is never recorded, because a stored snapshot goes stale between tranches and a ratchet on it would refuse an honest move of code between modules. Size the tranche from the newest main run's artifact, not from here. (3) YOU CANNOT MEASURE LOCALLY BELOW PYTHON 3.13.2 -- the pinned stubs will not install and the ruler refuses rather than measuring something else (#504). The programme box is 3.13.1. Expect to learn your error count from CI; budget for that round trip instead of discovering it. (4) by_code RATCHETS PER CODE AND A CODE THE CENSUS NEVER SAW HAS A BUDGET OF ZERO. Control: at a total held at exactly 516, moving one error from no-untyped-def to type-arg is REFUSED, and so is one new code. Partial annotation relabels rather than reduces, so a tranche that moves the total without moving the mix will fail; tighten every code you improved. (5) type_ignores IS A SEPARATE HARD METRIC AT 0, enforced in the fast job with no toolchain. --warn-unused-ignores cannot see a live ignore. # mypy: ignore-errors counts too, and a mypy config file is refused outright. (6) DO NOT PIN THE THIRD-PARTY REQUIREMENTS. homeassistant-stubs constrains the same packages; CI refused aiohttp==3.14.3 beside it as ResolutionImpossible. The pin is the mypy/stubs pair only, and the resolved versions are recorded in the census environment rather than asserted.

CARRIED FROM #540 (#524/#525): _shutdown_process_pool must NOT be called inline from a coroutine -- it is reaped at EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP on the executor, and the atexit backstop is left with nothing to wait for. Home Assistant's own loop-protection helper (upstream, not in this tree) compares the calling thread id against the loop's; time.sleep is protected and Popen.wait is not, but CPython's Popen._wait polls with time.sleep, which is why the detector fires. A coverage test that calls the reaper directly from async context will trip it. Also: tests/nightly_ha.py's KNOWN_BLOCKING now lists two offenders this fix removed, and Checks.check BLANKS the detail on pass, so the stale pin is SILENT -- a regression of either would pass the nightly (#533).
